# dsh-pi-ai-sync

A dsh Cordis plugin that keeps
provider routes in step with the pi.dev gateway by maintaining **both

** layers a
model has to pass through:

- the **pi-ai catalog** (`@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/data/<route>.json`)
— the "does dsh k

now this model and which protocol does it speak?" layer, and
- the **settings model list** (`llm-pi-

ai.providers.<route>.models`) — the
"does the model picker offer it?" layer.

It is the fusion of
`dsh-model-sync` (settings seam) and
`dsh-opencode-go-models`
(pi-ai catalog fil

e), with no hand-maintained protocol/family tables: pi.dev's
listing already carries every record in
pi-ai catalog shape.
## Why

dsh resolves a configured model's wire protocol as
`route.api ?? catalog[id].api ?? sharedCatalogApi

(route)`. On the dsh 0.1.x line
the settings model schema has **no per-model `api` field**, so:

- routes with a single protocol are fine — the route-level api fills the gap;
- a **mixed-protocol**

route (`opencode`: anthropic-messages +
openai-completions + openai-responses + google-generative-a

i) has no shared
api, so any model missing from the installed catalog is rejected outright:
hand-add
ing it errors, and a settings-only sync has to drop it.

`dsh-pi-ai-sync` fixes the root cause instead of working around it: it copies
the missing records in

to the installed catalog, then lets the (now complete)
catalog serve the route.
## How it works

A **layer** is where the data lives (the pi-ai catalog / the `llm-pi-ai`
settings); a round touches
both, in that order, for every managed route.

Because the catalog is imported into memory at boot, step 2 only takes effect
after a dsh restart —
a round that added models reports `restartNeeded`.
## Install
Not on npm yet — install it from GitHub today:

Restart dsh afterwards (bundle-layer change).
### GitHub installs need the build script allowed

A `github:` install runs the package's `prepare` script (never
`prepublishOnly`), because the TypeSc

ript sources are the only thing in the
repository — `lib/` is gitignored. pnpm blocks install-time s

cripts by default,
so add the key it prints to the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Use that form, not a bare `dsh-pi-ai-sync: true` (pnpm cannot match a name to a
git source) and not

the commit-pinned `…/tar.gz/<sha>` form pnpm's own error
message suggests — the pinned key goes stal

e on the next push, the `git+https`
key does not. dshmarket's "allow build scripts and retry" button

writes both
forms for you.

Integrity note: the tarball your install resolves to is the tag/commit you
asked for, and the build

happens on your machine from those sources. Use
`#vX.Y.Z` when you want a reproducible environment.
### Behind a proxy

This plugin reaches pi.dev with Node's global `fetch`, which **ignores**
`http_proxy` / `https_proxy

` unless Node is told to read them. On a network
that only reaches pi.dev through a proxy, a round f

ails with a bare
`TypeError: fetch failed` — and only sometimes, because the direct route is
usually
still there for other hosts. Start dsh with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

(`--use-env-proxy` is the same switch as a CLI flag.) `NO_PROXY` is honoured
either way. This is a h

ost setting on purpose: reading the environment from
inside the plugin would mean taking on an HTTP-

proxy dependency, and this
package has none.
## Configuration

Edit the `pi-ai-sync` section of your settings document (on the dsh 0.1.x line
that is `~/.dsh/setti

i-ai-sync` section of your settings document (on the dsh 0.1.x line
that is `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Key | Default | Description |

| `managedRoutes` | `[]` | Routes to sync; empty = `opencode`, `opencode-go` |
| `settingsMode` | `u
nset` | `unset` removes the route's `models` override; `mirror` rewrites it from pi.dev; `keep` leav

es settings alone |
| `catalogSync` | `true` | Maintain the installed pi-ai catalog files (the core

|
| `catalogSync` | `true` | Maintain the installed pi-ai catalog files (the core layer) |
[该节后续省略]
### Why some ids are "catalog-only"
Two lists move independently:

- the **catalog on disk** — the factory snapshot plus every id past rounds
merged in, and merges are

add-only;
- **pi.dev's live listing** — which gains and drops models over time.

An id the catalog has and pi.dev currently does not list is *catalog-only*. It
is not a pi.dev error

and nothing was deleted: the catalog is the union of
everything ever seen, so the two differ whenev

er pi.dev stops offering an id.
In practice that is mostly the promo `-free` and experimental `-exp`

models,
which rotate out — and the count moves on its own (observed: `opencode` at 85
ids, then 83,
twenty minutes later).

Removal is deliberately out of scope for v0.1: a partial pi.dev outage or a
bad network day must nev
er delete models from your picker.
## Caveats

- **The catalog layer writes into `node_modules`.** That is inherent: the
installed pi-ai catalog is

the only place dsh 0.1.x can learn a protocol for
a base-less model. Writes are atomic, a first-mod

ification backup is kept,
and a real uninstall restores it (a pi-ai upgrade that wholly replaces the

file is left untouched). A pi-ai upgrade wipes the additions; the next round
re-applies them.
- **A

round says why it gave up.** A failed fetch is retried `fetchAttempts`
times (default 3) with expon

ential backoff, then that route is skipped and the
report carries the whole cause chain — `fetch fai

led ← connect ETIMEDOUT
172.67.221.13:443` rather than a bare `fetch failed`. A 4xx other than 429 i

s
pi.dev answering, so it is not retried. Skipping is deliberate: **a route whose
listing could not

be verified keeps its settings untouched.**
- **Restart to see new models.** Catalog changes are rea

d at boot only.
- **Do not run this beside `dsh-model-sync` on the same routes.** One rewrites
`mode

ls`, the other unsets it. Pick one.
- **`mirror` + `modelOverrides`.** A route with non-empty `model

Overrides` is
skipped in `mirror` mode (folding/persisting overrides is `dsh-model-sync`'s
models-st
ore job). `unset` mode is unaffected and is the recommended default.
